assign.now: measured 12 pages x 2 widths (1280/3440) via getComputedStyle+canvas-advance probe in headless Chromium

log.msg: BLOCKS SAMPLED == ROWS IN JSON: 816 text blocks measured, 816 rows in type-raw.json (task dir), 0 probe errors across 12 pages x 2 widths. Prose-only tags (p/li/blockquote/dd/figcaption, excluding code/pre which double-count via pre>code nesting): 330 rows. Weight histogram (prose): 500=328 (99.4%), 700=2. Line-height ratio histogram (prose): 1.80=298 (90%), 1.45=30, 1.25=2 (all 3 buckets >=1.25, i.e. NO cramped <1.3 line-height found in real prose -- the site errs LOOSE not tight, opposite of the failure the brief worried about). Families seen across all 816 rows: only Montserrat and Consolas (the first item of --mono's fallback stack; code is set via font-family list Consolas/'Courier New'/Monaco/monospace and this Linux container almost certainly doesn't have Consolas installed, so getComputedStyle reports the AUTHORED first choice, not necessarily what glyphs actually paint -- a real cross-platform caveat, noted on the page).

MEASURE VERDICT: characters-per-line.md measured --measure at the OLD value 52em (83-108 chars). Live Page.css ships --measure:40em (changed 2026-08-17 per its own comment, replacing a wide-track cap measured 53% dead at 3440). Direct cpl measurement of real prose (p/li/blockquote/dd), filtering out single-line blocks where chars < cpl*1.3 (cpl is a canvas-advance extrapolation, meaningless for a line that never actually wrapped) found ZERO blocks over 95 chars across all 816 rows. p-tag cpl: 1280 median 80.5 (min 12.1 max 103.8 incl. non-wrapped outliers), 3440 median 80.9 -- viewport-invariant as the doc's own methodology predicts. Verdict: the doc is stale on the TOKEN's live value (52em->40em happened after it was written), not wrong about method; 40em already sits inside the classic 45-90 comfortable band, nearer the top (Bringhurst's 66 is tighter) than the ceiling.

HIERARCHY: framework.css base layer declares h3=1em/700 (same size as body) and h5/h6=1em/700 -- theme lew42.css overrides h1-h4 UPWARD (h1 3em/900, h2 2.25em/700, h3 1.5em/600, h4 0.875em/700 uppercase) but never touches h5/h6, which therefore ship at the base 1em/700 -- IDENTICAL, not just similar, to a bold/<strong> span in running prose (no strong/b rule anywhere in framework.css; browser default 700 applies). Confirmed both by CSS source and by rendering: framework/styles/elements/text/ page's own 'h5-h6' demo card shows h5, h6 and 'Body copy, for scale.' at visually indistinguishable size/weight (screenshot: shots/h5h6-fail.jpg). h5/h6 used only 3x each site-wide (near-dead code) -- real but low-blast-radius trap. Live ratios where the theme DOES reach: h1/h2=1.33x, h2/h3=1.5x, h3/body=1.5x -- all comfortably above the classic 1.2-1.333 minimum, nothing in the sanctioned ladder is hard to tell apart. Good specimens: scale-good.jpg (framework's own h1-h4-body demo card) and caption-vs-body.jpg (a blog post's bespoke byline 0.85em / standfirst 1.1em on top of the real h2/body ladder -- 4 distinct sizes in 6 lines).

assign.outcome: **One face (Montserrat, variable, loaded at runtime) for reading, a system-mono stack for code that is declared but never loaded — so what a reader sees for code depends on their OS. Line-height is loose (1.8 on 90% of prose), not cramped. `--measure` moved 52em→40em since `characters-per-line.md` was written; direct measurement of 816 real text blocks across 12 pages found zero prose lines over 95 characters — the doc is stale, not wrong. The one real hierarchy failure: h5/h6 ship at the framework's base 1em/700, pixel-identical to a bold sentence, because the theme overrides h1–h4 upward and never reaches them.** Landed: [Type study](/imagine/design/type/) — a live specimen sheet (real h1–h4/body/code/h5 elements, not screenshots), the measure verdict with a 45/66/95ch demo, the as-built hierarchy ratios (1.33×–1.5× everywhere the theme reaches, 1× where it doesn't), 3 captioned crops (1 failure, 2 good), and 3 concrete moves. Raw data: [type-raw.json](/framework/ai/2026-09-01/type-study/type-raw.json) (816 rows, 12 pages × 1280/3440, 0 errors). Left out: fixing h5/h6 itself (this is the study, not the patch); a caption/small-text step in the framework's own scale (proposed in the 3-moves paragraph, not built — a `.caption` class is a design decision, not this task's to make unasked).
